checks: If h+cL is concave, L+th=(1-ct)L+t(h+cL) is concave for small nonnegative t and stays positive by the uniform positive floor of L. One positive feasible t conversely gives c=1/t. This characterizes the radial cone, includes both affine signs and both signs of L, and positive scaling and addition preserve it. Uniform Taylor expansion uses bounded h/L and the original zero log mean.

The image of the radial cone and the open negative orthant are disjoint convex sets. A nonzero separating functional exists without closedness. Both scaling properties and 0 in the image force level zero. The functional is bounded above on the negative orthant, forcing nonnegative components, which can be normalized to sum one.

The resulting nonnegative pairing on the radial cone gives equal mass and full first moment by affine tests of both signs. The negative of any continuous convex test is admissible, giving the stated convex order in the correct direction. Direct use of the two density definitions makes both L integrals equal one.

The accepted compact coupling lemma applies in a Euclidean identification of the finite-dimensional affine space because all globally finite continuous convex tests restrict to the permitted tests on C. The positive finite atom at each distinct source has a conditional row with that barycenter. Repeated source locations can be split proportionally to the positive occurrence masses, which preserves the barycenter and all target marginals. The resulting submeasures are dominated by the target, so Radon–Nikodym densities give the stated allocations.

Concave Jensen bounds the L moment of each allocation by its atom mass times L_i. Equality of the totals forces equality in every positive row. The integral of the nonnegative gap of any touching affine majorant is then zero by the row barycenter. No existence of a touching majorant at arbitrary marks is needed.
